name: mutation-selection
description: A mutation may choose what it acts on. The judgement calls an engine has to make here are what this fixture pins down: UPDATE reaches mutable state and nothing else, a bounded sweep takes a documented order, a selection block reads the transaction's starting state, and a merge consolidates identity without copying or erasing anything.

cases.name: a sweep decays a Facet member by reading the target's own value
cases.command: UPDATE ?m SET FACET "MnemonicState" { memory_strength: MUL(?m.facets["MnemonicState"].memory_strength, 0.5) } WHERE { ?m CONCEPT {type: "Experience"} } LIMIT 2

cases.name: LIMIT cuts in ascending element id, so the same sweep twice takes the same elements
cases.command: FIND(?m.name, ?m.facets["MnemonicState"].memory_strength) WHERE { ?m CONCEPT {type: "Experience"} } ORDER BY ?m.name

cases.name: a Facet assignment merges members rather than replacing the Facet
cases.command: FIND(?m.facets["MnemonicState"].salience) WHERE { ?m CONCEPT {name: "First"} }

cases.name: UPDATE does not reach an Assertion's epistemic payload
cases.command: UPDATE ?a SET FIELDS { name: "relabelled" } WHERE { ?a ASSERTION {} }

cases.name: a selection block that matches nothing changes nothing, and does not create
cases.command: UPDATE ?m SET ATTRIBUTES { outcome_status: "aborted" } WHERE { ?m CONCEPT {type: "Experience"} FILTER(?m.attributes.goal == "no such goal") }

cases.name: a selection block reads the state the transaction started from
so the Concept the same transaction created is still in recall
cases.command: FIND(?m.name) WHERE { ?m CONCEPT {type: "Experience"} }

cases.name: a duplicate of the same person, recorded separately
cases.command: UPSERT CONCEPT ?dup { MATCH {type: "Person", key: "person:alice-duplicate"} SET FIELDS {name: "Alice"} }

cases.name: the upsert created the type its MATCH declared
cases.command: FIND(?p.name) WHERE { ?p CONCEPT {type: "Person", key: "person:alice-duplicate"} }

cases.name: a merge never picks an identity by description: two Concepts share the name
cases.command: MERGE CONCEPT ?source INTO ?target WHERE { ?source CONCEPT {key: "person:alice-duplicate"} ?target CONCEPT {name: "Alice"} }

cases.name: named by stable identity instead, the merge consolidates them
cases.command: MERGE CONCEPT ?source INTO ?target WHERE { ?source CONCEPT {key: "person:alice-duplicate"} ?target CONCEPT {key: "person:alice"} }

cases.name: a logical key is identity within its type
cases.command: UPSERT CONCEPT ?a { MATCH {type: "Person", key: "shared:label"} SET FIELDS {name: "A person"} }

cases.name: so another type may carry the same key, and it is a second identity
cases.command: UPSERT CONCEPT ?b { MATCH {type: "Option", key: "shared:label"} SET FIELDS {name: "A preference"} }

cases.name: the key alone now names two Concepts, and is not resolved arbitrarily
cases.command: UPSERT CONCEPT ?c { MATCH {key: "shared:label"} SET FIELDS {name: "?"} }

cases.name: an upsert declaring no type cannot create a Concept it would have to invent one for
cases.command: UPSERT CONCEPT ?x { MATCH {key: "person:nobody"} SET FIELDS {name: "Nobody"} }

cases.name: an upsert by id resolves only, so an id nothing carries is a failure and not a create
cases.command: UPSERT CONCEPT ?x { MATCH {type: "Person", id: "C-99999"} SET FIELDS {name: "Nobody"} }

cases.name: a MATCH member of the wrong type is refused rather than read as absent
cases.command: UPSERT CONCEPT ?x { MATCH {type: 42, key: "person:nobody"} SET FIELDS {name: "Nobody"} }

cases.name: MATCH selects; it does not seed the Concept it creates
cases.command: UPSERT CONCEPT ?x { MATCH {type: "Person", key: "person:unnamed", name: "Ignored"} }

cases.name: so grounding state arrives through SET FIELDS and nowhere else
cases.command: FIND(?p.key) WHERE { ?p CONCEPT {type: "Person", name: "Ignored"} }

cases.name: a name is not identity, and the language refuses it before an engine sees it
cases.command: UPSERT CONCEPT ?c { MATCH {type: "Person", name: "Alice"} SET FIELDS {name: "Alice B"} }

cases.name: and `_system` is engine state no mutation may name
cases.command: UPDATE "person:alice" SET FIELDS {_system: {version: 99}}

cases.name: a WHERE on a directly named target is a guard, and a guard that holds lets the write through
cases.command: UPDATE ?t SET FIELDS {name: "Alice Guarded"} WHERE { ?t CONCEPT {key: "person:alice"} }

cases.name: a guard that finds nothing makes the statement do nothing, and is not an error
cases.command: UPDATE ?t SET FIELDS {name: "Never"} WHERE { ?t CONCEPT {key: "person:alice"}  FILTER(?t.name == "Nobody") }

cases.name: so the guarded write landed and the unguarded one did not
cases.command: FIND(?c.name) WHERE { ?c CONCEPT {key: "person:alice"} }

cases.name: PURGE refuses by default while anything still references the target
cases.command: PURGE ?alice WHERE { ?alice CONCEPT {key: "person:alice"} } CONFIRM "PURGE"

cases.name: an unreferenced element erases, leaving an identity stub rather than a hole
cases.command: PURGE ?e WHERE { ?e CONCEPT {name: "Third", state: "archived"} } CONFIRM "PURGE"

cases.name: the stub keeps identity and a digest, and carries none of the content
cases.command: FIND(?e.name, ?e.governance.purged) WHERE { ?e CONCEPT {state: "purged"} }

Option.description: A preference option used by these fixtures. A real Space types each option by its kind (Profile §5.5, §7), because prefers partitions by the option's Concept Type; one catch-all type is one partition.
